To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the SMC head domains form an ABC ATP-binding cassette with a coiled-coil segment inserted between the N and C-termini, and that the N and C terminal globular domains come together to make a functional ABC ATPase.

we have solved the structure of the N and the C-terminal globular domain of SMC protein and that the structure of the S. maritima S. maritim SMC protein and the N-terminal domain of E. coli MukB is very similar to that of Rad50.

we determined the three-dimensional structure of the head domain of the SMC protein from Thermotoga marittima and found that it is closely related to other proteins involved in chromosome organization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of a large coiled-coils protein.
the structure, function and evolution of the bacterial SMC protein family.
the structure and function of the SMC protein family, which is involved in chromosome organization and repair.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SMC is an ABC ATPase.

the structure of SMChd represents the first structure of a SMC family member, which is the first structure of an ABC-ATPase family member with an inserted antiparallel coild-coil segment, and which is also the first structure of the MukBEF complex.
the structure of the S. maritima S. maritimam SMC head domain is an ABC ATPase that has an inserted 900 residue coile-coil and a hinge segment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have solved the structure of a protein that is a part of a larger protein, and that we have solved this structure by using the fact that the protein is a part of something bigger.
we solved the crystal structure and showed the mechanism for ATP binding and hydrolysis of SMC head domain.
we have shown that SMC proteins are ABC ATPases, and that the coiled coils are antiparallel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SMC coiled-coil is antiparallel, and the SMC N and C-terminal ATPase domains are closely related.
the ABC fold can accommodate a very large coiled-coils segment in the middle of its fold.
the coiled coil of the SMC protein is not just a long coiled coil, but rather a very special coiled coil with a special structure that is inserted into the middle of an ABC ATPase domain.
